questions.question: What should you do to avoid being an aggressive driver?

options.text: Plan trips without extra time for traffic.
Drive slowly in the left lane.
Do not make gestures at other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make gestures at other drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, plan trips with realistic time and extra time for traffic. Do not tailgate. Do not drive slowly in the left lane and do not make gestures at other drivers.

questions.question: When trailer air lines are color-coded, what color shows emergency lines?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: When trailer air lines are color-coded, blue is used for service lines and red is used for emergency lines.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Explain what you inspect and why.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you inspect and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do a complete inspection and explain to the examiner what you are checking and why.

questions.question: A stopped bus is:

options.text: Not a concern since it is stopped.
Only a concern if passengers are getting off.
Always a concern, whether or not you see passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always a concern, whether or not you see passengers.
questions.explanation: Always be careful near a stopped bus. Passengers may be nearby, and the bus may block your view of them or their view of you.

questions.question: If you see a large box in your lane ahead, you should:

options.text: Not worry because another vehicle will hit it first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful if you see objects in your lane. Even a cardboard box may contain heavy or hard items that could damage your vehicle.

questions.question: What can the "crack-the-whip" effect do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn over trailers.
questions.explanation: The "crack-the-whip" effect can cause a trailer to turn over during a lane change. Make lane changes slowly and safely to avoid this.

questions.question: Traction is important for:
questions.correctAnswerText: Safe braking.
questions.explanation: You cannot brake or steer without good traction. Check that your tires are in good condition before you drive.

questions.question: If your vehicle catches fire, you should not:

options.text: Park away from buildings, trees, brush, and other vehicles.
Tell emergency services about the fire and your location.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull into a service station.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire, leave the road and stop in an open area. Do not go to a service station because fuel there could catch fire. Call emergency services and tell them where you are.

questions.question: When driving in heavy traffic, you should:

options.text: Text instead of call on your cell phone.
Turn up your cell phone ringer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not use your cell phone.
questions.explanation: Heavy traffic, construction, many pedestrians, and bad weather all need your full attention. Avoid all distractions, including cell phone use.

questions.question: Your engine runs a pump for compressed gas delivery. After delivery, turn off the engine ____ unhooking the hoses.
questions.correctAnswerText: Before
questions.explanation: Turn off your engine when loading or unloading a compressed gas tank. If your engine runs a pump, turn it off after the transfer but before you unhook the hoses.

questions.question: When checking your vehicle, which of these should NOT worry you?

options.text: Exhaust parts rubbing against fuel system parts
Exhaust system parts that are leaking
Exhaust system parts made of aluminum

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust system parts made of aluminum
questions.explanation: When checking the exhaust system, look for loose, broken, or missing pipes, mufflers, or tailpipes. Also check for loose or missing brackets, clamps, bolts, or nuts. Watch for parts rubbing against fuel system parts, tires, or other vehicle parts. Look for leaking exhaust parts.

questions.question: People working on a broken-down vehicle:

options.text: May be focused on the repair and not notice traffic.
Do not have to follow traffic laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be focused on the repair and not notice traffic.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people working on a broken-down vehicle on the roadside. They may be focused on their repair and not paying attention to traffic around them.

questions.question: What does a material's hazard class tell you?

options.text: How fast the material must be delivered

questions.correctAnswerText: The dangers of the material
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are divided into nine hazard classes. A material's hazard class shows what dangers it poses.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a sign of bad brake drums or shoes?

options.text: Shoes that do not have brake fluid on them

questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes that do not have brake fluid on them
questions.explanation: When checking brakes, look for cracked drums. Check for shoes or pads with oil, grease, or brake fluid on them. Look for shoes that are missing, broken, or worn dangerously thin.

questions.question: Outage:

options.text: Is only a problem in hot weather.
Is the same for every liquid.
Should be considered when loading liquid into a tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be considered when loading liquid into a tank.
questions.explanation: Liquids expand when they get hot. Empty space must be left in a tank for this expansion. This space is called "outage." Different liquids need different amounts of outage.

questions.question: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, do all of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: Take your foot off the brake pedal.
Turn quickly in the direction of the skid.
Countersteer once the vehicle is straight again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, first take your foot off the brake so the locked wheels can roll again. Turn quickly in the direction you want to go. Then countersteer to stop the vehicle from skidding the other way.

questions.question: While driving:

options.text: You cannot send a text, but you can read one.
You can send a text, but you cannot read one.
You cannot send or read a text.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot send or read a text.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is not allowed. Texting means typing words into a device or reading words from a device.

questions.question: Keeping cargo low can:
questions.correctAnswerText: Help prevent a rollover.
questions.explanation: A vehicle can roll over if you turn too quickly. To reduce the risk of rollover, keep the center of gravity low by loading cargo as close to the ground as possible.

questions.question: To help control liquid surge, you should:

options.text: Stay closer to the vehicle in front of you.
Start braking early before you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start braking early before you stop.
questions.explanation: Drive vehicles with unbaffled tanks slowly and carefully, especially when stopping and starting. Brake early before you stop and stay farther back from the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: Turn the top of the wheel in the direction you want the trailer to go.
Turn the top of the wheel in the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to go.
It depends on where you are backing the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the top of the wheel in the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to go.
questions.explanation: When backing a trailer, turn the top of the steering wheel in the opposite direction of where you want to go. Once the trailer starts turning the right way, switch the steering wheel direction to follow the trailer.
